title: Mishra, Gayen & Naveira Garabato (2026): Reversal of Antarctic Intermediate Water trends triggered by sea ice decline
materials: Press coverage only (Scientific Frontline, Oceanographic, Phys.org screenshot). Paper, figures, salinity/density magnitudes, depths and methods NOT read. Related: Spira et al. 2026 (Nature Climate Change, doi:10.1038/s41558-026-02601-4), open-access PDF read through a fetch tool. Unit conversions computed in earth-systems-physics aaiw_reversal_2026.py.
decision_context: User-chosen study, routed to Thwaites and Earth-system modelling: whether a Southern Ocean freshwater budget built around ice-shelf melt (the CDW-AABW loop in earth-systems-physics, the Thwaites audit in CEED) needs the sea-ice meltwater term, and whether AAIW has changed state. No decision owner named.

tools.output: Type EMPIRICAL (observational trend analysis plus attribution). Material is press coverage; method-level checks are NOT_CHECKED rather than passed.

4 claims. Conditional form of C2: IF the meltwater figures are net freshwater delivered to the AAIW source region AND no other freshwater term moved enough to cancel, THEN reduced sea-ice melt explains the reversal.

Unit conversion (earth-systems-physics aaiw_reversal_2026.py): drop 6,600 km3/yr = 0.209 Sv, a third of the pre-2016 figure. That is about 63x the CDW-attributable ice-shelf basal melt (104.8 Gt/yr) the repo's CDW-AABW loop runs on. Each budget carries one of two freshwater terms that moved in opposite directions over the same years.

Related, not independent of the trigger: Spira et al. 2026 (same journal) study the same 2015-16 sea-ice drop and attribute it to wind-driven mixing. The two papers agree on the event and sit at different links of one chain: wind -> mixing -> sea ice -> meltwater -> AAIW.

Open branches for the AAIW reversal: (a) reduced sea-ice meltwater (paper); (b) wind and Ekman-transport changes acting directly on AAIW formation; (c) multi-year internal variability over a 9-year window; (d) change in data coverage. Cheapest discriminator: compare the post-2016 trend with all earlier 9-year windows of the same record.

Term frame: 'healthy' AAIW is defined by the 1995-2015 state (A1). A baseline taken from one window is a reading of that window; 'reversal' is measured against it. The past-transition comparison sets a 9-year trend beside a completed state change (C4).

Target: has AAIW changed state, and why? Rendering: 'reversed', 'triggered by sea ice decline', 'may have underestimated'. Observed: a trend change over 9 years. Attribution and the sea-level implication are not checkable at press depth.

decisions.text: Add the sea-ice meltwater term beside ice-shelf melt in Southern Ocean freshwater budgets (earth-systems-physics CDW-AABW loop, CEED Thwaites audit). Does not depend on C2's attribution, only on the term being large and moving.
Treat AAIW as having changed state (tipping) rather than as a multi-year excursion? Depends on C1 against earlier windows and on internal variability, not in the material read.

design_checks.finding: One water mass, 1995-2024, reversal window 2016-2024 (9 years). The coverage calls it the first direct observational evidence. Argo near-global coverage is a 2000s development, so the early part of the 1995-2015 baseline rests on sparser data (VERIFY in the paper).

The meltwater comparison (about 3x then 2x the Amazon's annual flow) is a melt volume. Sea ice that forms and melts in place delivers no net freshwater over a year; whether the figure is gross seasonal melt or net delivery to the AAIW source region is not stated in the material read.

The coverage names sea-ice decline as the trigger and does not mention ice-shelf (glacial) meltwater, which other work in the same period reports rising. Spira et al. 2026 attribute the 2015-16 sea-ice drop itself to wind-driven mixing over thinned Winter Water, so the 'trigger' is one link in a chain.
No uncertainties, magnitudes or depths in the material read.
Observational analysis of a natural record.
